key_idea: Condition on the last ball: it must be one of the 2n card numbers and its partner must be undrawn, while the first p-1 balls (as a set from the other m-2 numbers) must cover the remaining n-1 squares.
sketch: Count sets of p-1 numbers out of the m-2 others that hit each of the n-1 other squares: sum over j squares with both numbers drawn of C(n-1,j)*2^(n-1-j)*C(m-2n, p-n-j). The probability is 2n*count / (m*C(m-1,p-1)); reduce with gcd. Everything fits in 64 bits for m<=33 (count <= C(31,k)). Pitfalls: n=0 wins only when p=0 (answer 1/1), p<n gives 0/1, print 0/1 for zero. Verified against a permutation brute force for all m<=7.
